title: Dual scalar comparisons of lines and signed tensor and tower coherence
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site with finite limits and final object, small relative to the sheaf universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Let $R_0\xrightarrow{\iota_{01}}R_1\xrightarrow{\iota_{12}}R_2$ be commutative ring sheaves and $\iota_{02}=\iota_{12}\iota_{01}$. Let $L_i$ be $R_i$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], each locally isomorphic to $R_i$ on a covering of the final object. Suppose given isomorphisms $b_{ij}:L_i\otimes_{R_i}R_j\xrightarrow{\sim}L_j$ for $i<j$, with $b_{02}=b_{12}(b_{01}\otimes1)$ under tensor reassociation. Use sheaf tensor and sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-pur-sheaf-hom], and write $L_i^{[0]}=R_i$, $L_i^{[n]}=L_i^{\otimes n}$ and $L_i^{[-n]}=\mathcal Hom_{R_i}(L_i^{[n]},R_i)$ for $n>0$. For $m\geq0$ let $b_{ij,m}$ be the unit and recursively induced tensor-power comparisons of $b_{ij}$. For $n>0$ the formula
$$\beta_{ij,n}(\varphi\otimes s)(x\otimes t)=\iota_{ij}(\varphi(x))st$$
defines an isomorphism
$$\mathcal Hom_{R_i}(L_i^{[n]},R_i)\otimes_{R_i}R_j\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal Hom_{R_j}(L_i^{[n]}\otimes_{R_i}R_j,R_j).$$
Set $b_{ij,-n}(\varphi\otimes s)=\beta_{ij,n}(\varphi\otimes s)\circ b_{ij,n}^{-1}$. These signed-power isomorphisms commute with evaluation, in the precise sense
$$\operatorname{ev}(b_{ij,-n}(\varphi\otimes s),b_{ij,n}(x\otimes t))=\iota_{ij}(\varphi(x))st.$$
For $a,b\in\mathbf Z$ there is a canonical isomorphism $\mu_i^{a,b}:L_i^{[a]}\otimes_{R_i}L_i^{[b]}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_i^{[a+b]}$, normalized by $e_i^a\otimes e_i^b\mapsto e_i^{a+b}$ for every local basis $e_i$ of $L_i$; negative powers of a basis mean its dual powers. It is the map given by tensor associativity, symmetry and evaluation contractions. If $\sigma_{ij}$ is the canonical scalar/tensor comparison, then
$$b_{ij,a+b}\circ(\mu_i^{a,b}\otimes1)=\mu_j^{a,b}\circ(b_{ij,a}\otimes b_{ij,b})\circ\sigma_{ij}.$$
For every integer $m$, the maps satisfy
$$b_{02,m}\circ\mathrm{ass}=b_{12,m}\circ(b_{01,m}\otimes1),$$
where $\mathrm{ass}:((M\otimes_{R_0}R_1)\otimes_{R_1}R_2)\xrightarrow{\sim}M\otimes_{R_0}R_2$ sends $(x\otimes s)\otimes t$ to $x\otimes\iota_{12}(s)t$ and has inverse $x\otimes t\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes t$. For identity ring maps equipped with the multiplication comparison at exponent one, every $b_{ii,m}$ is the tensor-unit comparison. On any compatible local bases $e_j=b_{ij}(e_i\otimes1)$ the formula for every signed exponent is $b_{ij,m}((r e_i^m)\otimes s)=\iota_{ij}(r)s e_j^m$.

proof.text: Work on the localized sites of a covering $\{U_\lambda\to1\}$ trivializing a line. Restriction commutes with sheaf tensor, including change of rings, by [lem-sfb-localized-site-tensor-restriction], and with sheaf Hom by its slice definition [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. By [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing], maps agreeing on the pairwise fiber products glue uniquely. In particular, equality of two global module maps can be checked on this cover: both are the unique gluing of the same restrictions. A map with inverses on the cover is invertible globally: on overlaps two local inverses $v,w$ of $f$ satisfy $v=vfw=w$, hence glue, and the two inverse identities hold by the same uniqueness. All pullbacks of the cover exist by finite limits, so this applies over every object of the site, without assuming enough points.

On a chart with basis $e$ for $L$, the tensor unitors of [lem-sp-scalar-extension-binary-coherence] identify $L^{[n]}$ with $R$ by the basis $e^n$ for $n\geq0$ (start at $1\in R$ and tensor one more $e$). For $n>0$ the slice definition of Hom identifies its dual with $R$: a functional is determined by $c=\varphi(e^n)$, and is $re^n\mapsto rc$. Thus $e^{-n}$ is the functional taking $e^n$ to $1$. These identifications hold on every object over the chart, and commute with restriction. If $e'=ue$ is another basis, its coordinate $u$ is a unit since the inverse basis change supplies $u^{-1}$. Tensoring gives $(e')^n=u^ne^n$, while evaluating on $(e')^n$ gives $(e')^{-n}=u^{-n}e^{-n}$. Consequently $(e')^m=u^me^m$ for every integer $m$.

source.place: Tags 03EK (section-tensor-product) and 04TT (section-internal-hom), unitors and local rank-one coordinates.

proof.text: Use the scalar/tensor and unit comparisons of [lem-sp-scalar-extension-binary-coherence], exchanging the two tensor factors to use the statement's right-hand scalar convention. The exchange is $s\otimes x\mapsto x\otimes s$, with inverse the same exchange, by the bilinear universal property. The unit comparison is $r\otimes s\mapsto\iota_{ij}(r)s$. For a local basis $e_i$, the scalar extension of its chart is a free $R_j$-module with basis $e_i\otimes1$, so $e_j=b_{ij}(e_i\otimes1)$ is a basis. The recursive positive-power map is an isomorphism, being a composite of the binary comparison and tensors of the given isomorphism. Induction, with exponent zero the unit comparison, proves that $b_{ij,m}((re_i^m)\otimes s)=\iota_{ij}(r)s e_j^m$ for every $m\geq0$: the induction step sends the pure basis tensor to $e_j^m\otimes e_j=e_j^{m+1}$ and linearity supplies its coefficient.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), scalar tensor formula and its bilinear universal property; recursive tensor powers.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sp-scalar-extension-dual-evaluation] to $N=L_i^{[n]}$. In the right-hand scalar convention it constructs exactly $\beta_{ij,n}$ with evaluation $\iota_{ij}(\varphi(x))st$ on $x\otimes t$, on every slice. To check it is invertible, choose the chart of step 2. The source has basis $(e_i^n)^\vee\otimes1$ by the scalar unit comparison. The target has basis the functional sending $e_i^n\otimes1$ to $1$ by the slice Hom definition. The evaluation formula sends the former basis to the latter. The local inverse sends a functional $h$ to $((e_i^n)^\vee\otimes1)h(e_i^n\otimes1)$. These are inverse maps on every object over the chart. The local inverses glue by step 1, giving an isomorphism without any flatness assumption on $R_i\to R_j$.

source.place: Tag 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom), specialized to change of rings; Tags 03EK, 04TT and 03EM for the local inverse.

proof.text: Precomposition with $b_{ij,n}^{-1}$ is an isomorphism on sheaf Hom: its inverse is precomposition with $b_{ij,n}$, by the slice definition. Hence the stated definition of $b_{ij,-n}$ is an isomorphism. Evaluation at $b_{ij,n}(x\otimes t)$ cancels this inverse, leaving exactly $\beta_{ij,n}(\varphi\otimes s)(x\otimes t)=\iota_{ij}(\varphi(x))st$. In compatible bases, this says $b_{ij,-n}((re_i^{-n})\otimes s)$ evaluated at $e_j^n$ is $\iota_{ij}(r)s$; a functional on a free line is determined by that value. This proves the displayed local formula for every negative exponent, completing all signed exponents.

source.place: Tag 0GMX (remark-pullback-internal-hom), evaluation; Tag 04TT (section-internal-hom), precomposition on slices.

proof.text: For any integers $a,b$ define on a basis chart the bilinear map $(re^a,qe^b)\mapsto rq e^{a+b}$. By [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] this defines a linear map from the sheaf tensor, and its inverse in these coordinates is $ce^{a+b}\mapsto(ce^a)\otimes e^b$. To compare charts put $e'=ue$. The map normalized using $e$ sends $(e')^a\otimes(e')^b$ to $u^au^b e^{a+b}=u^{a+b}e^{a+b}=(e')^{a+b}$, including negative $a,b$ since $u$ is a unit. Thus the chart maps and inverses agree on overlaps. By [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] they glue to an isomorphism $\mu_i^{a,b}$. The normalization determines it uniquely, since on every chart its domain is a free line generated by $e^a\otimes e^b$.

source.place: Tags 03EK (section-tensor-product), bilinear universal property; 03EM (lemma-internal-hom), via Sites 04TQ (lemma-glue-maps), gluing.

proof.text: Verify the contraction description without choosing additional data. Put $D=\mathcal Hom_R(L,R)$. The pairing of pure tensors $d_1\otimes\cdots\otimes d_n$ and $x_1\otimes\cdots\otimes x_n$ with value $\prod_k d_k(x_k)$ gives a map $D^{\otimes n}\to\mathcal Hom_R(L^{\otimes n},R)$ by the bilinear universal property and the slice definition of Hom. It is an isomorphism: on each basis chart it sends $(e^\vee)^{\otimes n}$ to $e^{-n}$, and the inverse chart maps glue as in step 1. For $a,b\geq0$ concatenate the $L$ factors. For $a,b\leq0$ concatenate the $D$ factors using these identifications. For $a=p\geq0$, $b=-q\leq0$, reassociate and exchange factors, evaluate $\min(p,q)$ pairs $e^\vee\otimes e$, and retain the remaining $L$ factors if $p\geq q$ or $D$ factors otherwise. For $a\leq0$, $b\geq0$ first exchange the two blocks and use the same construction; exponent zero uses a unitor. Every evaluation contributes $1$, so each such map sends $e^a\otimes e^b$ to $e^{a+b}$. Uniqueness in step 6 identifies these maps with $\mu_i^{a,b}$.

source.place: Tags 03EK and 04TT, tensor and evaluation on slices; Tag 0FNY (example-dual), local dual-basis pairing, with the rank-one verification written here.

proof.text: The normalized binary scalar comparison of [lem-sp-scalar-extension-binary-coherence] is, in our tensor order, $\sigma_{ij}((x\otimes y)\otimes s)=(x\otimes s)\otimes(y\otimes1)$. Check the desired multiplication square over a chart of $L_i$, using $e_j=b_{ij}(e_i\otimes1)$. Its source is a free $R_j$-line with basis $((e_i^a\otimes e_i^b)\otimes1)$. More explicitly, on $((re_i^a\otimes qe_i^b)\otimes s)$ the left route gives $\iota_{ij}(rq)s e_j^{a+b}$; the right route gives $\iota_{ij}(r)s\,\iota_{ij}(q)e_j^{a+b}$. These are equal because $\iota_{ij}$ preserves products. This calculation uses the already proved formula for all signed $a,b$ and $a+b$, so includes every mixed-sign case. Linearity gives equality on the whole chart and the uniqueness in step 1 gives equality globally.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), normalized scalar/tensor comparison; signed-power basis calculation.

proof.text: For completeness the coefficient associator used in the tower is defined on pure tensors by $((x\otimes s)\otimes t)\mapsto x\otimes\iota_{12}(s)t$. This respects the inner $R_0$ balance since $\iota_{02}(r)=\iota_{12}(\iota_{01}(r))$, and respects the outer $R_1$ balance since $\iota_{12}(ss')t=\iota_{12}(s)\iota_{12}(s')t$. The sheaf bilinear universal property therefore constructs it. Its inverse is $x\otimes t\mapsto(x\otimes1)\otimes t$, which respects $R_0$ balance using the same coefficient equation. The first composite fixes $x\otimes t$. The second sends $((x\otimes s)\otimes t)$ to $(x\otimes1)\otimes\iota_{12}(s)t=((x\otimes s)\otimes t)$ by the outer balancing relation. Equality follows by the universal property's uniqueness, iterated over the two tensors. Thus this is the asserted isomorphism for arbitrary $M$, not just for lines.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), bilinear universal property and ordinary change-of-rings associativity.

proof.text: Choose a basis $e_0$ on a trivializing cover and put $e_1=b_{01}(e_0\otimes1)$ and $e_2=b_{12}(e_1\otimes1)$. The hypothesis at exponent one implies also $e_2=b_{02}(e_0\otimes1)$. For every integer $m$, the left route in the tower equation sends $((re_0^m\otimes s)\otimes t)$ to $\iota_{02}(r)\iota_{12}(s)t e_2^m$. The right route sends it to $\iota_{12}(\iota_{01}(r)s)t e_2^m$. Multiplicativity and the composite-ring-map hypothesis identify these coefficients. The source is a free $R_2$-line on the iterated extension of $e_0^m$, so this gives the tower equality on the chart; step 1 gives it globally. Finally take the identity ring map with $b_{ii,1}(x\otimes s)=sx$. The compatible basis is then $e_i$ itself. For every signed $m$ the formula already proved reads $(re_i^m)\otimes s\mapsto rs e_i^m$, which is exactly the tensor-unit comparison. Local equality and gluing prove this globally, including $m=0$.

split_report.blueprint: prop-weil-twist-preserves.proof.md: the sentence that twists are tensor powers and internal Homs, and the last sentence about levelwise and common finite stages. Steps 2-7 construct signed comparisons and contractions, step 8 checks tensor compatibility, steps 9-10 give coefficient towers and identities.

tool_uses.why: Uses only the ordinary sheaf tensor bilinear universal property to construct and compare the local pairings and balanced coefficient associator; the unit has no such universal-property node.
Uses restriction of the actual sheaf tensor to arbitrary localized sites, preserving pure sections, to compute on a basis cover; this is generic sheaf infrastructure absent from the unit.
Uses existence and uniqueness of gluing linear maps on one cover, both for basis-independent products and inverse maps; this generic locality theorem is not a step replacing the unit route.

Uses only normalized binary tensor, unit and scalar comparisons, with their section formulas, to induce positive powers and compute the tensor square; the signed powers and tower equalities are proved here.
Uses the canonical ordinary dual evaluation map and its section formula, not any signed-power or tower assertion; its rank-one inverse is proved here.
